methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements that capture a single aspect of the design or functionality.
mindtraced_atomic_units: D flip-flops have active high asynchronous reset
Output should be reset to 0 when areset is high
D flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk
8-bit input 'd' provides the data input to the eight D flip-flops, such that d[0] is the D input to q[0], d[1] is the D input to q[1], and so on.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, d[7:0], and areset
areset is an active-high asynchronous reset
When areset is high, output q is immediately reset to 0
clk is the clock input for the D flip-flops
d input provides the data to be stored in the flip-flops
q output holds the stored data
Combinational logic ensures that when areset is high, q is forced to 0
areset signal has the highest priority
When areset is high, the output q[7:0] is immediately set to 8'b0
The design uses an always block triggered by the positive edge of clk or the positive edge of areset
Inside the always block, an if statement checks if areset is high
If areset is high, q is reset to 0 using a non-blocking assignment
Otherwise, q is assigned the value of d using a non-blocking assignment
There are eight D flip-flops implemented using the 8-bit vector q
The flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk
